A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimuHome simulator and benchmark. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures and equations, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 16 agents on 600 episodes, plus error analyses, framework comparisons, feedback experiments and Gemma fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and supplementary results and reports comparisons including two fine-tuned agents.

M1.justification: The core simulator and ReAct procedure persist, but Table 6 changes reported capabilities: for example, RVC Run Mode's Start/Stop/Map/StopMap becomes ChangeToMode. v3 also supplies more specific environmental dynamics. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences reflect operational changes or corrections and additions to the implementation description.

E1.justification: Both retain the 600-episode smart-home benchmark and the 204-trajectory fine-tuning dataset. The six query types with feasible and infeasible variants represent the same twelve categories despite renamed scheduling types. No additional domain, population or task scenario is reported.

E2.justification: v3 adds Qwen3-32B (SFT) and includes Gemma3-4B-it (SFT) in the full Table 1 comparison. v2 reported Gemma's fine-tuned variant separately on five feasible categories in Appendix H. The original 16 agents and the ReAct–HiAgent comparison remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds a larger-model fine-tuning control, comparing Qwen3-32B with Gemma3-4B-it trained on the same 204 trajectories. The existing benchmark evaluation procedures remain. Newly specified optimization parameters and five-minute self-review callbacks document settings without establishing changes to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning analysis expands from small-model memorization resistance to comparisons across model sizes and feasible versus infeasible requests. Conversely, v2 Appendix E.3's breakdown of API error categories for four models is removed. HiAgent, self-review, multi-turn feedback, failure-notice recovery and the three-second evaluation-delay analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both report three judge queries per episode, seed-controlled episode generation and the same agreement statistics: 0.92 for query validation, 0.913 between human judges and 0.826 for judge–human agreement. v3 clarifies aggregation as majority voting. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated model-run information.

E6.justification: The original 16-model scores and latency values remain unchanged. v3 adds complete Qwen3-32B SFT results, including 26%, 20% and 12% on feasible QT4-1/2/3, and additional Gemma SFT results. Table 11 changes contradiction-mishandling counts for QT2 and QT4-1/2/3 from 24/5/6/1 to 23/4/7/2, aligning totals with Table 1. Figure 7's API-error results disappear.

T1.justification: v2's POMDP formulation in Section 3.3 is removed. Its generic additive aggregator equation in Appendix P is substantially expanded in v3 Appendix E into baseline-reversion dynamics, humidity and PM10 bounds, and a separate non-accumulating illuminance equation. These materially revise the formal specification; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The simulator and benchmark contributions remain. v3 drops v2's explicit promise of near drop-in transfer to physical Matter devices and qualifies the blanket reasoning-model superiority claim by emphasizing uneven scheduling gains. Its abstract and conclusion foreground persistent scheduling difficulties and the fine-tuning findings.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive fidelity boundaries: Appendix C excludes transport security, commissioning and fabric management, while Appendix E describes a simplified environmental model intended for qualitative agent evaluation. Section 5.4 additionally explains stronger fine-tuning gains on infeasible requests through their shared verification-and-refusal structure. These substantially qualify applicability and extend the interpretation of results.

D1.justification: v3 replaces a promised future release with a code/data availability statement. It adds environmental constants and update ordering, revised capability inventories, five-minute callback details, and SFT settings: Adam, learning rate 5e-5, batch size 1, three epochs and one H200 GPU. However, six judge prompts present in v2 are omitted and referred to the repository, reducing PDF-contained reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 characterizes embodied benchmarks as addressing a different problem and acknowledges SAGE's dynamically changing device settings, narrowing the claimed gap to environmental effects, operational dependencies and scheduling. It removes several general tool-agent citations and adds Wang et al. (2023) for self-consistency and Zheng et al. (2023) for LLM judging.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, simulator description, benchmark explanation and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Analysis subsections are reorganized, appendices are substantially reordered, and terminology is standardized around six query types, twelve evaluation categories, prerequisite actions and workflow scheduling.

P2.justification: Most figures retain their original designs. v3 redraws Figure 4, removes Figure 7, moves the latency table beside Table 1, and relocates Figure 6 and the self-review table to Appendix M. It also incorporates SFT rows, introduces a twelve-category SFT delta display, and reformats and consolidates appendix tables.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the simulator's assumptions and experimental setup easier to assess, qualifies overly broad transfer claims, extends fine-tuning evidence beyond a small model, and corrects inconsistent error totals. These provide a supported quality gain while the central benchmark evidence remains stable. Removing six judge prompts and the detailed API-error analysis reduces self-contained auditability, limiting the net improvement.
